inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 170.75M Class A + 0.03M Class 1 outstanding at 2026-06-26 (Q1 FY27 10-Q cover) plus ~0.22M dilutive awards (Q1 FY27 diluted 172.407M vs basic 172.186M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting as well would double-charge it.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $67.7M + payments of minimum tax withholdings on stock-based awards $9.4M (no combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation figure published). Interest income not stripped: STZ is ~$10.5B net debt, interest expense is reported net.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 (staples beverage alcohol with discretionary premium-import tilt) -> cost of equity ~8.8%. Pre-tax debt ~4.6% (mostly fixed-rate senior notes), ~3.6% after tax. Market weights: ~$10.5B debt vs ~$19.3B equity (35/65) -> ~7.0%; rounded up to 7.5% for single-country (Mexico) production and trade-policy exposure. Same WACC in every scenario: demand and tariff risk are carried in the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): US GAAP operating-lease cost (noncash lease expense $127.4M FY26) already sits inside COGS/SG&A and therefore inside EBITDA; operating lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path left at 0 to avoid charging the lease twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of the Mexican glass-plant JV and other non-wholly-owned entities). NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at ~11x FY26 NCI earnings of $70.1M (distributions $62.5M).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 2: US consumer operating company with moderate cyclicality). STZ is a producer/importer of Mexican beer plus a small wine & spirits segment - not a bank/REIT/holdco/LIC; FCF is a real operating stream. First valuation of STZ (no MEMORY entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2026 (ended 2026-02-28): revenue $9,139.0M (Beer ~$8.3B, W&S ~$0.82B after the 2025 Wine Divestitures). Adjusted EBITDA FY26 = op income 2,721.4 + D&A 420.0 + asset impairment 109.8 + loss on sale 31.9 + SBC 67.7 = $3,350.8M (36.7%). Year-1 (FY27) margin set at 36.5% to absorb restructuring cash costs and to reconcile with guidance: guided FCF $1.6-1.7B (OCF $2.4-2.5B less ~$0.8B capex) + ~$270M after-tax interest - $77M SBC implies ~$1.84B unlevered owner FCF; the component build gives ~$1.92B. Revenue path starts at -1.5% for FY27: guided organic (1)% to +1% plus the Q1 lap of the 2025 Wine Divestitures (Q1 FY27 net sales -3.3% YoY) - the shrinking W&S mix is not extrapolated as a flat company growth rate. Capex ~9.2% FY27 (beer ~$800M Mexican brewery capacity) glides to ~5.5% (just above D&A ~5%) once Nava/Obregon expansion completes. Cash tax: FY26 taxes paid were only $173.6M (~7% of pretax) on DTA unwind from the intra-entity IP transfer and OB3 bonus depreciation; modelled at 17% FY27 rising to 20% by FY30 - the shelter is NOT perpetuated into the terminal year. Canopy Growth: FY24-FY25 impairments ($511.8M equity losses FY24, $76.1M FY25 exchangeable-share write-down) and the FY25 $2.8B W&S goodwill impairment are non-cash and non-recurring; excluded from run-rate. Exchangeable shares carried at $21.2M added in the bridge. Net debt = short-term borrowings 336.3 + current LTD 1,102.6 + LTD 9,094.9 - cash 96.6 = $10,437.2M at 2026-05-31, plus $100.0M of buybacks executed between 1 June and 26 June 2026 (debt-funded) so net debt matches the 26 June share count -> $10,537.2M. Buybacks: $924.1M FY26, $223.8M Q1 FY27 - the flat count is funded by real repurchases ($2.75B left on the $4.0B authorization). Q2 FY27 results due 2026-10-06 after close: re-anchor FY27 growth/margin then.

equity_bridge.note: FY26 10-K: NCI net income $70.1M x ~11; book NCI $304.5M understates the earnings claim
FY26 10-K Note 11: 26.3M exchangeable shares carried at $21.2M fair value; non-operating, no income in flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-9.6% 5yr) is not usable: book value was shrunk by ~$4.6B of buybacks FY22-FY26 and by the FY25 $2.8B W&S goodwill and FY23-FY25 Canopy impairments. EPS 3yr CAGR undefined (FY23 GAAP EPS -0.11). Revenue 5yr CAGR understates Beer's organic growth (mid-single-digit until FY25) because the Wine Divestitures removed ~$0.8B of revenue; selected 1.2% only as the historical anchor - the scenario paths are built bottom-up.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding (no interest income stripped; net debt company). FY21 1,871.2, FY23 1,642.6, FY26 1,716.9. Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported within 0.1pp: SBC (~0.8% of revenue) is not the story at STZ; capex intensity (brewery build) and the divested wine mix are.

base.narrative: Flagship softness bottoms in FY27-28; growth brands (Pacifico, Victoria, Chelada) restore low-single-digit beer growth; restructuring savings lift op margin into the guided 32-33% band; capex normalises once Mexican capacity lands.

bull.narrative: Hispanic consumer spending normalises and Modelo/Corona depletions return to growth while the smaller brands keep compounding double-digit; beer back to mid-single-digit; operating leverage plus restructuring and a premiumised W&S push margins above the guided band.

bear.narrative: Flagship decline is structural (Hispanic demand, moderation/GLP-1, cannabis and spirits substitution); Modelo/Corona keep shrinking faster than the growth brands can offset; fixed brewery cost deleverages and aluminum tariffs persist; W&S keeps declining at 5-6% margins.

scenario_narratives.base: Beer depletions stop falling in FY28 as Pacifico, Victoria and Modelo Chelada keep taking share and flagship Modelo Especial/Corona Extra flatten; enterprise revenue dips ~1.5% in FY27 (flat organic plus the Wine Divestitures lap) then recovers to 2-3%. Comparable operating margin settles in the guided 32-33% band (adj. EBITDA ~38%) as 2025 restructuring savings land, and capex falls from ~9% of sales to ~5.5% once the Mexican brewery build completes, lifting owner FCF from ~$1.9B to ~$2.4B by FY31.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Hispanic-consumer soft patch proves cyclical (immigration-enforcement fear and value-seeking ease), the April 2026 malt-beverage tariff carve-out holds, and the new CEO sharpens price-pack architecture and W&S premiumisation. Beer returns to 4-5% growth, margins reach ~39.5% adj. EBITDA, and the $4.0B buyback compounds per-share value from a ~10x earnings base.
scenario_narratives.bear: The flagship decline is structural rather than cyclical: Modelo Especial and Corona Extra keep losing volume to moderation, spirits/RTDs and cannabis while the core demographic stays under pressure, and smaller brands are too small to offset. Revenue falls two years running, fixed-cost deleverage and 50% aluminum tariffs hold adj. EBITDA at ~35%, leverage pins near 3.0x, and trade policy towards Mexico remains a recurring tail.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the demand problem sits in the flagship brands and the core demographic with no visible catalyst, a CEO transition is under way, and 100% of beer is made in one country exposed to US trade policy. Base 50% reflects a franchise still holding #1 dollar share with intact pricing. Bull cut to 25% because it needs two independent things - a Hispanic-consumer recovery and flagship stabilisation - to go right together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mature staples-like cash generator priced as if the flagship decline is permanent. Owner FCF on a fully expensed SBC basis (SBC is small, ~0.85% of sales), unlevered flows at a 7.5% USD WACC, NCI deducted once, terminal capped at 13-17x to stop Gordon from paying a perpetuity multiple a buyer need not grant. The swing factors are beer volume and the capex fade, not accounting.
key_risks_to_valuation: Modelo Especial / Corona Extra depletion declines prove structural (base assumes they flatten by FY28)
US trade policy on Mexican imports: malt-beverage tariff carve-out reversed, or aluminum tariffs raised further
Capex fails to fade to ~5.5% of sales (another capacity round) - each 1pp of sales is ~$90M/yr of FCF
Cash tax rises faster than the 17%->20% ramp as the DTA shelter runs off
Leverage ~3.0x net debt/EBITDA: equity is ~65% of EV so every 10% move in EV is ~15% per share
Q2 FY27 results (2026-10-06) may reset FY27 guidance; this build is anchored to the July 2026 guide
